A **dental bone graft** is a procedure where your dentist/oral surgeon adds bone or bone-like material to part of your jaw to **build up or replace missing bone**. Over time, your body grows new bone into that area, creating a stronger foundation.

You may need one before a **dental implant** because an implant is like an artificial tooth root: it must be anchored firmly in the jawbone. If the jawbone is **too thin, too short, too soft, or has shrunk**, the implant may not be stable enough or may have a higher risk of failure. Mayo Clinic notes that if the jawbone isn’t thick enough or is too soft, bone grafting may be needed before implant surgery. ([mayoclinic.org](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/dental-implant-surgery/about/pac-20384622?utm_source=openai))

Common reasons there may not be enough bone include:

- **Tooth loss over time** — bone shrinks when there’s no tooth root stimulating it.
- **Gum disease/periodontitis** — can destroy the supporting bone.
- **Infection or abscess**
- **Trauma or difficult extraction**
- **Upper back teeth** — the sinus may be close to the implant site, so a sinus lift/bone graft may be needed. The American Academy of Periodontology notes the upper back jaw can be difficult due to limited bone and closeness to the sinus. ([perio.org](https://www.perio.org/for-patients/periodontal-treatments-and-procedures/dental-implant-procedures/?utm_source=openai))

The graft material can come from several sources: your own bone, donor bone, animal-derived bone, or synthetic material. The purpose is to **increase bone volume and improve implant stability**. Cleveland Clinic says dental bone grafts can increase eligibility for dental implants and other restorative treatments. ([my.clevelandclinic.org](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/21727-dental-bone-graft?utm_source=openai))

In some cases, the graft and implant can be done **at the same appointment**. In other cases, the graft needs to heal first — often for several months — before the implant is placed.

A simple way to think of it: **the implant needs enough “ground” to hold onto.** The bone graft is done to rebuild that ground so the implant has a better chance of lasting. Ask your dentist to show you on your X-ray/CBCT scan exactly where the bone is lacking and whether your graft is minor, major, or a sinus-related graft.

In Singapore, **you usually don’t “claim” MediSave yourself after wisdom tooth surgery**. The **MediSave-accredited dental clinic / hospital submits the claim for you**, after you authorise it with a **Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF)**.

## Step-by-step: claiming MediSave for wisdom tooth surgery

### 1. Confirm it is **wisdom tooth surgery**, not simple extraction
MediSave is generally claimable only if the removal is a **surgical procedure** done for medical reasons — e.g. impacted/partially erupted wisdom tooth requiring incision, bone removal, stitches, etc. **Simple non-surgical extraction is usually not MediSave-claimable.** CPF states that wisdom tooth removal can be paid using MediSave if it is a surgical procedure; non-surgical dental services are generally not covered. ([ask.gov.sg](https://ask.gov.sg/cpf/questions/cm0f52l0201n9pz7a1ef50rye?utm_source=openai))

### 2. Choose a **MediSave-accredited** clinic/hospital
Before booking, ask the clinic clearly:

> “Are you MediSave-accredited, and can you submit the MediSave claim for wisdom tooth surgery?”

MOH lists MediSave-accredited institutions as including public hospitals, private hospitals, polyclinics, MediSave-accredited GP clinics, and **MediSave-accredited dental clinics**. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medisave/))

### 3. Ask for a cost estimate and claimable amount
Ask the clinic for:

- Total estimated bill per tooth  
- Whether it is **surgical** and MediSave-claimable  
- Estimated MediSave claim amount  
- Expected cash top-up, if any  
- Whether X-rays, consultation, medication, GST, sedation/GA are included  
- Whether the claim is under **day surgery** and which surgical table/ranking applies

For day surgery, CPF states you can use MediSave for **up to $830 per day** for ward/day-surgery charges and **$240 to $5,290** for the surgical procedure, depending on the type/complexity of surgery. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-medisave-can-i-use-to-pay-for-my-own-or-an-approved-dependant-s-day-surgery-bills?utm_source=openai))

### 4. Check whose MediSave you are using
You can use:

- Your own MediSave; or  
- An approved dependant’s / family member’s MediSave, where allowed.

MOH says approved dependants include **spouse, parent, grandparent, sibling, and child**; grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medisave/))

### 5. Complete the **Medical Claims Authorisation Form — MCAF**
At the clinic/hospital, tell the counter staff you want to use MediSave. You and the MediSave account holder, if different from the patient, must authorise the claim.

CPF says if you intend to use MediSave, you need to complete the **Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF)** and authorise the medical institution to submit the claim on your behalf. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-is-the-medical-claims-authorisation-form-mcaf))

For most private dental clinics, you will likely complete **MCAF(S)** for that treatment/visit. MOH notes that **MCAF(S)** is used if you are visiting a non-public healthcare institution or prefer authorisation at each visit; if using your MediSave for a family member, you must use **MCAF(S)**. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medisave/))

### 6. Bring the required documents
Usually bring:

- NRIC / FIN  
- CPF/MediSave account holder details if using someone else’s MediSave  
- Referral letter, if going through public route  
- Dental X-ray/OPG if already taken  
- Company/insurance forms, if you also plan to claim from employer or private insurance

### 7. Do the surgery
The dentist/oral surgeon performs the wisdom tooth surgery. The clinic will prepare the final bill and submit the MediSave claim electronically.

### 8. Pay any balance not covered by MediSave
MediSave will cover only up to the allowed withdrawal limit and not more than the actual bill. Any remaining amount — for example, consultation, X-ray, medication, GST, sedation/GA, or charges above the MediSave limit — must be paid by cash/card/other insurance.

### 9. Check your CPF MediSave deduction
After the claim is processed, check your CPF transaction history to confirm the amount deducted from MediSave. If you paid a deposit and MediSave later covers more than expected, the clinic may refund the excess according to their billing process.

### 2) **Surgical/impacted wisdom tooth removal — usually MediSave, not CHAS for the surgery item**
If it’s surgical — e.g. impacted wisdom tooth requiring gum incision/bone removal/tooth division — you can use **MediSave**, provided the procedure is done at a MediSave-accredited/participating clinic and is a surgical procedure. MediSave is not a discount; it pays from your CPF MediSave account. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/can-i-use-medisave-to-pay-for-the-removal-of-my-wisdom-tooth))

For many single impacted wisdom tooth surgeries under local anaesthesia, the **cash out-of-pocket can be $0** if the clinic’s bill is within the applicable MediSave claim limit and you have enough MediSave balance. But your **MediSave balance will be deducted**.

MOH’s public-institution average fees for impacted wisdom tooth surgery under local anaesthesia are about **$784–$1,319 before GST**, generally excluding consultation/X-ray/investigation fees. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/bills-and-fee-benchmarks/guide-to-dental-treatment-costs/))

**Cash you pay now = Clinic bill − CHAS subsidy − MediSave used**

**Clinic bill − CHAS subsidy**, because MediSave is still your own CPF money.

## Complete guide to Invisalign in Singapore — updated 22 September 2026

### Quick take

**Invisalign** is a doctor-supervised clear-aligner system used to move teeth gradually with a sequence of removable plastic trays. In Singapore, it is usually considered an **elective orthodontic treatment**, so you should expect to pay privately. The official Invisalign Singapore page says prices **start from about S$3,400 for simple cases**, while current Singapore clinic fee guides commonly place Invisalign from roughly **S$3,900–S$9,800+**, and some market guides quote up to **S$13,500+ before GST** for comprehensive/specialist or complex cases. ([invisalign.com.sg](https://www.invisalign.com.sg/cost-page))

---

# 1. What Invisalign is

Invisalign is a brand of **clear aligners**: custom-made trays that fit over your teeth and are changed in sequence to move teeth gradually. HealthHub describes clear-aligner therapy as removable clear plastic overlays that “grip” the teeth to move them into desired positions; SingHealth similarly describes clear aligners as removable braces worn full-time and removed for eating and brushing. ([healthhub.sg](https://www.healthhub.sg/health-conditions/dental-braces))

Unlike fixed metal or ceramic braces, Invisalign is removable. This makes eating and cleaning easier, but it also means the treatment depends heavily on your discipline: many Singapore clinic guides advise **20–22 hours of wear per day**, removed only for meals, non-water drinks, brushing and flossing. ([neosmiles.com.sg](https://neosmiles.com.sg/invisalign-cost-singapore/))

---

# 2. Who Invisalign is suitable for

**Often suitable for:**

- Mild to moderate crowding  
- Gaps between teeth  
- Minor relapse after previous braces  
- Some bite issues, depending on severity  
- Adults or teens who want a less visible orthodontic option  

HealthHub notes that clear aligners are the least visible and comfortable orthodontic option, but says they are generally for **moderate alignment issues**; SingHealth says clear aligners are good for **less severe cases**, and that your orthodontist is best placed to recommend the right system for your malocclusion. ([healthhub.sg](https://www.healthhub.sg/health-conditions/dental-braces))

**May be less suitable if you have:**

- Severe crowding or bite discrepancy  
- Major jaw-size discrepancy  
- Teeth needing large vertical movements  
- Impacted teeth  
- Poor gum health or active decay  
- Low likelihood of wearing aligners 20–22 hours daily  
- A case requiring jaw surgery or complex extractions  

That does **not** mean Invisalign can never handle complex cases; it means you need a proper orthodontic assessment. For severe skeletal or bite problems, fixed braces, surgery, or a combined approach may be more predictable.

---

# 3. Invisalign vs braces in Singapore

| Factor | Invisalign | Metal / ceramic braces |
|---|---|---|
| Visibility | Very discreet | Metal visible; ceramic less visible |
| Removable | Yes | No |
| Eating | Remove trays; fewer food restrictions | Avoid hard/sticky foods |
| Cleaning | Easier to brush/floss teeth, but must clean trays | More difficult around brackets/wires |
| Discipline needed | Very high — wear time matters | Less dependent on patient remembering to wear appliance |
| Complex movements | Case-dependent | Often better for complex movements |
| Comfort | Usually no brackets/wires; pressure with each tray | Bracket/wire irritation possible |
| Visits | Often every 4–8 weeks or longer depending on protocol | Usually regular adjustments |
| Cost | Often comparable or higher | Usually lower to mid-range, depending on type |

MOH’s dental cost guide lists average **non-subsidised public-institution fees for non-surgical two-jaw braces** from about **S$3,930 to S$5,800**, excluding GST and generally excluding consultation, x-rays, investigations and re-treatment fees; this is for braces, not Invisalign, but it is a useful benchmark when comparing orthodontic quotes. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/bills-and-fee-benchmarks/guide-to-dental-treatment-costs/))

---

# 4. Typical Invisalign cost in Singapore

### Official starting price

Invisalign Singapore says treatment **starts from S$3,400 for simple cases**, and that the cost depends on case complexity, treatment duration and provider. ([invisalign.com.sg](https://www.invisalign.com.sg/cost-page))

### Common 2026 private-clinic ranges

Current Singapore clinic guides show a wide spread. For example, Advanced Dental lists Invisalign packages around **S$3,900–S$7,900**, while Neo Smiles lists **S$7,000–S$9,800** depending on condition and needs. A 2026 market guide by Dentalis lists approximate market ranges of **S$1,888–S$4,800 for Express**, **S$3,400–S$6,500 for Lite**, **S$5,800–S$8,500 for Moderate**, and **S$6,500–S$13,500+ for Comprehensive**, before GST. ([advanceddental.co](https://www.advanceddental.co/procedures/invisalign/cost/))

### Practical budget guide

| Case type | Rough Singapore budget |
|---|---:|
| Very minor relapse / limited front-tooth correction | S$3,400–S$5,000+ |
| Mild case | S$4,000–S$6,500+ |
| Moderate case | S$6,000–S$8,500+ |
| Comprehensive / complex case | S$7,000–S$13,500+ |
| Retainers after treatment | Often extra; ask specifically |

The quoted “package” may not include everything. Common extras include consultation, x-rays, 3D scan, ClinCheck planning, extractions, interproximal reduction, attachments, refinements, emergency visits, replacement aligners, whitening, and retainers. One Singapore clinic guide gives an example where retainers are billed separately and can range from lower-cost Essix retainers to higher-cost Invisalign Vivera retainers. ([advanceddental.co](https://www.advanceddental.co/procedures/invisalign/cost/))

---

# 5. Can you use CHAS, MediSave or insurance?

### MediSave

Generally, **no** for Invisalign. CPF states that non-surgical dental services, including orthodontic braces, are not covered by MediSave; Invisalign is an orthodontic aligner treatment, so you should assume it is not MediSave-claimable unless your dentist identifies a separate surgical procedure that qualifies. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/10-uses-of-medisave?utm_source=openai))

### CHAS

Generally, **no** for Invisalign itself. MOH’s CHAS dental subsidy table covers listed procedures such as consultation, extraction, fillings, dentures, crowns, root canal treatment, scaling, polishing, fluoride and x-rays; orthodontic aligners/braces are not listed in the CHAS dental subsidy table. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/chas/))

### Corporate dental benefits / insurance

Some corporate plans may cover consultation, x-rays or routine dental cleaning, but most will not fully cover orthodontics unless orthodontic benefits are explicitly included. Always ask your HR/insurer for pre-authorisation before starting.

---

# 6. The Invisalign process in Singapore

## Step 1 — Initial consultation

Your dentist or orthodontist checks your teeth, gums, bite, jaw relationship, dental history and goals. Expect photos, x-rays and/or a 3D scan if you proceed. Invisalign’s own doctor-locator page describes doctor-led care as involving a precise 3D scan, analysis of the scan, and progress monitoring throughout treatment. ([invisalign.com](https://www.invisalign.com/find-a-doctor))

## Step 2 — Records and diagnosis

This may include:

- Intraoral scan or impressions  
- OPG x-ray  
- Cephalometric x-ray, especially for bite/jaw cases  
- Photos  
- Bite analysis  
- Gum and decay check  
- Wisdom-tooth or missing-tooth assessment  

This stage is important because moving teeth when gums are unhealthy or decay is untreated can create bigger problems.

## Step 3 — Digital treatment plan

Your provider creates a digital plan showing proposed tooth movements. Invisalign cases are planned using staged aligner movements; clinics may show you a simulation, but the simulation is not a guaranteed final result. The important question is whether the planned movements are biologically realistic and stable.

## Step 4 — Review the quotation

Before paying a deposit, clarify whether your quote includes:

- Consultation  
- X-rays  
- 3D scan  
- ClinCheck planning  
- All aligners  
- Attachments  
- Interproximal reduction, if needed  
- Refinements  
- Mid-course correction  
- Retainers  
- Replacement aligners  
- Emergency visits  
- GST  
- Payment-plan fees  

## Step 5 — Aligner fitting

You receive your first trays. Your dentist may place small tooth-coloured **attachments** on certain teeth to help the aligners grip and move them more predictably. You may also need **IPR** — careful polishing between selected teeth to create tiny amounts of space.

## Step 6 — Active treatment

You wear each set of aligners as instructed, commonly changing trays every 1–2 weeks depending on your plan. Review intervals vary, but Singapore clinic guides commonly describe in-person reviews every few weeks to a few months; Dentalis’ 2026 guide notes review intervals of around **3–8 weeks**, while Neo Smiles describes regular review appointments about **6–8 weeks** apart. ([dentalis.clinic](https://www.dentalis.clinic/invisalign-singapore-guide/))

## Step 7 — Refinements

Many people need refinements: extra aligners after the initial set to fine-tune tooth positions. Refinements are common and not necessarily a sign of failure. The key is whether refinements are included, capped or charged separately.

## Step 8 — Retainers

After active treatment, you need retainers. SingHealth notes that after orthodontic treatment, retainers are needed to hold teeth in their new positions, and that adult patients are often prescribed night-time retainer wear long term if they want to maintain perfect alignment. ([singhealth.com.sg](https://www.singhealth.com.sg/patient-care/conditions-treatments/crooked-and-poorly-aligned-teeth-malocclusion))

---

# 7. How long Invisalign takes

Invisalign Singapore states that Invisalign averages **12–18 months**, while Invisalign Go may be as little as 6 months for simple-to-moderate front-tooth cases. ([invisalign.com.sg](https://www.invisalign.com.sg/cost-page))

A practical range in Singapore:

| Case | Approximate duration |
|---|---:|
| Minor relapse | 2–4 months |
| Mild crowding/spacing | 4–9 months |
| Moderate case | 9–18 months |
| Comprehensive case | 18–30 months |
| Complex bite / extraction case | 24+ months possible |

HealthHub gives a broader orthodontic-treatment average of **15–24 months**, depending on tooth movement, complexity, attendance and compliance. ([healthhub.sg](https://www.healthhub.sg/health-conditions/dental-braces))

---

# 8. Daily life with Invisalign

### You must wear the aligners almost all day

Most providers advise **20–22 hours/day**. If you wear them less, teeth may not “track” properly, treatment may take longer, or refinements may be needed. ([neosmiles.com.sg](https://neosmiles.com.sg/invisalign-cost-singapore/))

### Eating and drinking

Remove aligners for:

- Food  
- Coffee/tea  
- Sweet drinks  
- Alcohol  
- Anything hot  
- Anything staining  

Plain water is usually fine with aligners in.

### Cleaning routine

You should:

- Brush after meals before reinserting trays  
- Floss daily  
- Rinse aligners when removed  
- Clean aligners gently  
- Avoid hot water, which can warp trays  
- Keep aligners in their case, not tissue paper  

### Speech

A slight lisp is common for the first few days, and usually improves as your tongue adapts.

### Pain or pressure

Mild pressure is normal when starting a new tray. Sharp pain, persistent ulcers, cracked aligners or trays that do not seat properly should be reviewed.

---

# 9. Risks and limitations

Invisalign is generally safe when properly planned and monitored, but it is still orthodontic treatment. Possible issues include:

- Tooth sensitivity  
- Gum soreness  
- Ulcers or aligner irritation  
- Attachments falling off  
- Teeth not tracking  
- Bite changes during treatment  
- Need for refinements  
- Root resorption, rarely  
- Gum recession in susceptible patients  
- Cavities or staining if hygiene is poor  
- Relapse if retainers are not worn  

Poorly aligned teeth can be harder to clean and may contribute to decay or gum problems, but orthodontic treatment is still elective for many people; SingHealth notes that the best type of brace should be advised by an orthodontist based on your teeth and needs. ([singhealth.com.sg](https://www.singhealth.com.sg/patient-care/conditions-treatments/crooked-and-poorly-aligned-teeth-malocclusion))

---

# 10. Dentist vs orthodontist in Singapore

In Singapore, Invisalign may be provided by a general dentist trained in aligner treatment or by a registered orthodontic specialist. For simple cases, a general dentist with strong Invisalign experience may be appropriate. For complex crowding, extractions, bite correction, jaw discrepancy, previous failed orthodontics, gum issues or treatment for children/teens, it is sensible to consult an orthodontist or at least get a second opinion.

The Singapore Dental Council says all dental practitioners must be registered and hold a valid practising certificate before practising dentistry in Singapore, and the SDC website provides a register search for dentists and oral health therapists. ([sdc.gov.sg](https://www.sdc.gov.sg/))

### How to verify your provider

Before committing:

1. Search the dentist on the **Singapore Dental Council register**.  
2. Check whether they are a general dentist or registered orthodontic specialist.  
3. Ask how many similar Invisalign cases they have treated.  
4. Ask to see before/after examples of cases similar to yours.  
5. Ask who will review you at each visit.  
6. Ask what happens if teeth do not track.  

Invisalign “provider tiers” can be useful but should not be your only criterion. Some clinic guides note that Invisalign tiers are based mainly on case volume, not necessarily individual clinical skill or outcome quality. ([dentalis.clinic](https://www.dentalis.clinic/invisalign-singapore-guide/))

---

# 11. Invisalign vs other clear aligners in Singapore

There are other clear-aligner brands in Singapore, including clinic-branded aligners and regional/global alternatives. They may be cheaper, but compare carefully.

Ask:

- Is it dentist-supervised or remote-only?  
- Are x-rays taken before treatment?  
- Who plans the tooth movement?  
- Can the system handle bite correction or only front teeth?  
- Are attachments and IPR available?  
- Are refinements included?  
- Are retainers included?  
- What happens if treatment fails?  
- Is the provider registered with SDC?  

Invisalign’s official Singapore page distinguishes Invisalign from Invisalign Go and “most other clear aligners sold online,” saying Invisalign can cover simple to complex full-arch movements including bite correction, while Invisalign Go is for simple-to-moderate “social smile” movement of front teeth. ([invisalign.com.sg](https://www.invisalign.com.sg/cost-page))

---

# 12. Red flags when comparing quotes

Be cautious if:

- The clinic gives a quote without x-rays or proper assessment  
- The package price excludes many essentials  
- Retainers are not discussed  
- Refinements are expensive or unclear  
- You are promised a perfect result  
- The simulation is presented as guaranteed  
- You never see the dentist after the first visit  
- The provider dismisses gum disease, decay or bite problems  
- The quote is far cheaper but excludes attachments, refinements or reviews  
- You are pressured to sign immediately  

MOH advises patients to ask what procedures are required, whether alternatives exist, what the expected fee range is, what the cost breakdown is, and whether there are additional charges. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/bills-and-fee-benchmarks/guide-to-dental-treatment-costs/))

---

# 13. Questions to ask at your consultation

Bring this checklist:

### Diagnosis

- What is my orthodontic problem: crowding, spacing, overbite, underbite, crossbite, open bite?
- Is my case mild, moderate or complex?
- Do I need extractions?
- Do I need wisdom-tooth removal first?
- Are my gums healthy enough for orthodontics?
- Is Invisalign the best option, or would braces be more predictable?

### Treatment plan

- How many aligners are expected?
- How long will treatment take?
- Will I need attachments?
- Will I need IPR?
- How often are reviews?
- Who will see me at each review?
- What happens if teeth do not track?

### Cost

- Is the price before or after GST?
- Are x-rays included?
- Is the 3D scan included?
- Is ClinCheck planning included?
- Are refinements included?
- How many refinements are included?
- Are retainers included?
- What retainer type is provided?
- What is the cost of replacement aligners?
- Is there an instalment plan?
- What happens if I transfer clinics or move overseas?

### Aftercare

- How long must I wear retainers?
- How much do replacement retainers cost?
- Are retainer reviews included?
- What if my teeth relapse?

---

# 14. Best candidates for Invisalign

You are likely a good candidate if:

- Your case is mild to moderate  
- Your gums and teeth are healthy  
- You can commit to 20–22 hours/day  
- You want a discreet option  
- You are willing to remove trays before eating/drinking  
- You can attend reviews consistently  
- You understand refinements may be needed  
- You are willing to wear retainers long term  

You may be better suited to braces or a specialist opinion if your case is severe, your bite is unstable, you need extractions, you have significant jaw discrepancy, or you know you will not wear aligners consistently.

---

# 15. Bottom line

Invisalign in Singapore is convenient, discreet and effective for many cases, but it is not simply a cosmetic product — it is orthodontic treatment. Budget realistically, compare **total all-in cost**, verify your provider, and do not choose based on the cheapest headline price alone.

If you want the safest approach: get **two consultations** — one from an Invisalign-heavy provider and one from an orthodontist — then compare diagnosis, treatment plan, inclusions, refinement policy, retainer plan and total cost.

**Short answer: No — a beautician in Singapore generally cannot legally administer Botox/botulinum toxin injections.** MOH states that medical procedures such as **fillers or botulinum injections must be performed only by Singapore Medical Council-registered medical practitioners**, and by/through healthcare service providers licensed under the Healthcare Services Act (HCSA). Beauty salons are outside the HCSA licensing regime. ([moh.gov.sg](https://www.moh.gov.sg/newsroom/non-licensed-healthcare-entities-not-permitted-to-make-advertising-claims/))

A Botox injection is also the kind of procedure that involves **puncturing the skin to inject a substance**, which falls within the HCSA concept of a “clinical procedure”; MOH says aesthetic procedures that are clinical procedures may only be provided by a licensee and performed by registered doctors/dentists/oral health therapists, as applicable. Beauty salons or aesthetic providers may be prosecuted if they perform such procedures without the proper licence and personnel. ([sso.agc.gov.sg](https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/HSA2020?ValidDate=20231219&utm_source=openai))

**Practical distinction:**
- If a **beautician personally injects** the Botox: **not legal / major red flag**.
- If a beautician at a salon says a “doctor supervises” remotely but the beautician injects: **still a red flag**.
- If you are at a **licensed medical/dental clinic** and the injection is done by an appropriately registered practitioner with the required competence: that is the lawful route. SMC also has specific aesthetic-practice guidelines and competence requirements for doctors performing aesthetic procedures. ([smc.gov.sg](https://www.smc.gov.sg/for-professionals/regulations-guidelines-circulars/guidelines-on-aesthetic-practices-for-doctors/))

HSA has also warned that DIY injectable kits, dermal fillers and botulinum toxin products should be administered by qualified medical practitioners, and that illegal/unapproved products can carry serious risks. ([hsa.gov.sg](https://www.hsa.gov.sg/announcements/hsa-removes-over-3-000-online-listings-of-illegal-health-products-in-first-joint-operation-with-online-platforms/))

**What to do before booking:**
1. Ask: “Who will actually inject me — full name and registration number?”
2. Check the person is a registered doctor via the official healthcare professional directory.
3. Check the premises is a licensed healthcare service provider/clinic.
4. Avoid home-based or salon-based injectable offers, especially if they are unusually cheap or marketed on social media.

- [ ] **Tell your dentist/oral surgeon about:**
  - All medications and supplements you take.
  - Blood thinners, aspirin, diabetes meds, steroids, or immune-suppressing meds.
  - Drug/latex allergies.
  - Pregnancy or possible pregnancy.
  - Medical conditions such as asthma, heart disease, sleep apnea, bleeding disorders, diabetes, or past anaesthesia problems.
- [ ] **Ask what medicines to stop or continue.** Do not stop prescription medicines unless your doctor/dentist tells you to.

**Ultherapy（常被叫“美版超声刀”）**是一种非手术医美提升治疗，属于**微聚焦超声 + 实时影像（MFU‑V）**技术。它把超声能量打到皮肤较深层（真皮/筋膜浅层等目标层），造成可控的热凝固点，刺激胶原收缩和新生，从而达到**轻度到中度的紧致、提拉**效果。它不是开刀拉皮，效果通常比较自然、渐进，适合轻中度松弛；如果皮肤松垂很明显，效果一般不如手术拉皮。官方新加坡页面也说明，结果通常在治疗后 **2–3个月**逐渐明显，维持时间因人而异，可达 **12–18个月**。([ultherapysg.com](https://www.ultherapysg.com/faqs.html))

## 常见副作用

多数是短暂、轻中度的：

1. **治疗时疼痛/酸胀/刺痛**  
   打能量时会有痛感，部位不同、能量不同、个人耐受不同，感觉差异很大。

2. **发红、发热**  
   通常数小时内缓解；官方资料提到治疗后可能有轻微发红。([ultherapysg.com](https://www.ultherapysg.com/faqs.html))

3. **肿胀、触痛、压痛**  
   可能持续几天，有些人下颌线、颈部会觉得酸胀或按压痛。官方资料也列出轻微肿胀、刺麻、触痛等暂时反应。([ultherapysg.com](https://www.ultherapysg.com/faqs.html))

4. **淤青、麻木、刺麻感**  
   新加坡 NEA 对 HIFU 类设备的说明提到，可能出现治疗中/后疼痛、水肿、淤青、刺麻、红斑等；多数已报告的不良反应是暂时性的，约一周左右缓解。([nea.gov.sg](https://www.nea.gov.sg/our-services/radiation-safety/radiation-safety-information-for-apparatus-used-in-beauty-and-medical-aesthetic-industry/information-on-high-intensity-focused-ultrasound-apparatus))

5. **暂时性神经反应**  
   例如局部麻木、表情不对称、嘴角/眉毛短暂无力等，通常少见且多为暂时性；Ultherapy 官方 IFU 页面也列出临床试验中常见副作用包括红肿、疼痛和“暂时性神经影响”。([ultherapy.com](https://ultherapy.com/ifu))

## 少见但需要重视的风险

- **烫伤、水泡、结痂**  
- **皮下硬结、条索感**  
- **局部脂肪减少/凹陷、脸颊变瘦或不平整**，尤其是能量层次或部位选择不当时  
- **色素沉着或肤色不均**  
- **效果不明显或左右不对称**  
- **疼痛或麻木持续较久**  

一项关于 MFU‑V 的系统综述/荟萃分析认为，该治疗总体安全性较好，但常见不良反应包括红斑、水肿、肿胀、淤青和触痛，多数为轻到中度；同时疼痛感通常不能完全忽略。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11834976/?utm_source=openai))

## 在新加坡做要注意什么

- **Ultherapy 是品牌名**，不是所有“HIFU/超声刀”都等于 Ultherapy。市面上有很多 HIFU 设备，能量、探头、影像定位、安全性和效果都不同。  
- 尽量选择**正规医疗机构、注册医生**，并确认是否为官方认证设备/诊所。新加坡 MOH 说明，涉及美容的“clinical procedure”应由持牌机构并由注册医生、牙医或相关注册专业人士提供；无牌美容院/服务商若进行此类程序可被处理。([ask.gov.sg](https://ask.gov.sg/moh/questions/clu6lx3re007g314r6j9paoez))  
- 做前问清楚：  
  1. 是不是 **Ultherapy / Ultherapy PRIME 正品设备**？  
  2. 谁操作？医生是否全程评估和操作？  
  3. 打哪些层次、多少发数、哪些部位不打？  
  4. 你的脸型是否有脂肪少、凹陷、神经敏感等风险？  
  5. 如果出现烫伤、麻木、面部不对称，诊所如何处理？

## 谁要特别谨慎？

如果你有**活动性皮肤感染、开放伤口、严重痤疮发炎、近期做过填充/线雕/手术、面部神经问题、严重瘢痕体质、植入物、怀孕或哺乳**等情况，建议先让医生评估，不要直接做。

**一句话总结：**Ultherapy 是一种非手术提拉紧肤的微聚焦超声治疗，适合轻中度松弛；常见副作用是疼、红、肿、触痛、麻刺和淤青，多数短暂，但也有少见的烫伤、神经反应、凹陷或不对称风险。选择正规医生和正品设备很重要。

- Payroll and payslips
- CPF calculations/submissions
- Leave and attendance tracking
- Claims and reimbursements
- Onboarding/offboarding
- Performance reviews
- HR documents and policy acknowledgements
- Reporting for compliance, finance, and management

## Does a small company in Singapore need one?

**Not always — but it often becomes useful earlier than founders expect.**

For a very small company, say **1–4 employees**, you can usually manage HR with spreadsheets, calendar reminders, CPF EZPay, and standard templates — provided someone is disciplined about payroll, leave, payslips, and record-keeping.

But in Singapore, even small employers still have legal/admin obligations. For example, employers must issue itemised payslips to employees covered by the Employment Act and keep payslip records; MOM also requires employers to keep employee records such as name, address, earnings, and deductions. ([mom.gov.sg](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/itemised-payslips)) ([mom.gov.sg](https://www.mom.gov.sg/faq/contract-of-service/what-employee-records-do-i-need-to-keep)) CPF contributions are due at the end of the calendar month, with enforcement action possible if payment is not made by the 14th of the following month. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/making-cpf-contributions))

A Singapore small company should **seriously consider an HRIS** when it has:

- **5 or more employees** — especially because IRAS Auto-Inclusion Scheme participation is compulsory for employers with 5 or more employees, and once registered, annual electronic submission is mandatory. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/employers/auto-inclusion-scheme-%28ais%29-for-employment-income/join-the-auto-inclusion-scheme-%28ais%29-for-employment-income))
- Part-timers, shift workers, overtime, or commission-based pay
- Frequent leave, claims, or reimbursement admin
- Foreign employees or tax clearance matters
- Multiple managers approving leave/claims
- A founder or office manager spending too much time on manual HR
- A need for clean records for audits, grants, investors, or due diligence

## Practical rule of thumb

| Company size | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **1–4 employees** | HRIS optional. Spreadsheets + CPF/IRAS/MOM tools may be enough. |
| **5–10 employees** | Strongly consider a basic payroll/HRIS system, especially AIS-ready payroll. |
| **10+ employees** | HRIS is usually worth it for time savings, compliance, and cleaner records. |
| **20+ employees** | You probably need one unless HR is outsourced completely. |

## My recommendation

For a small Singapore company, you do **not necessarily need a full HRIS immediately**, but you should at least use a **basic payroll/leave system** that can handle:

1. CPF calculations  
2. Itemised payslips  
3. Leave balances  
4. Employee records  
5. IRAS AIS submission, if applicable  
6. Claims/reimbursements, if relevant  

If you are below 5 employees and have simple salaries, a lightweight tool or outsourced payroll provider may be enough. If you are at or approaching 5 employees, I would choose an HRIS/payroll system now rather than rebuilding everything later.

## 1) Confirm your CPF setup before touching Xero

You’ll need:

- **CPF Submission Number (CSN)** — CPF Board says you need a CSN to submit CPF contributions. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/making-cpf-contributions))  
- Employee details: **NRIC/FIN, date of birth, citizenship/PR status, PR conversion date if applicable, salary, allowances, bonuses, start date**.
- Correct CPF rates: CPF applies to **Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents** earning more than $50/month, and rates vary by **age, citizenship/PR year, and wage band**. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay))  
- Correct wage classification: e.g. salary, overtime, bonuses, allowances and commissions can attract CPF, while genuine reimbursements and benefits-in-kind generally should not be included as wages. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/what-payments-attract-cpf-contributions))

For Singapore Citizens and SPRs from the **third year onward**, with monthly wages above $750, the **2026 CPF rates** are: under/at 55: **17% employer + 20% employee**; above 55–60: **16% + 18%**; above 60–65: **12.5% + 12.5%**; above 65–70: **9% + 7.5%**; above 70: **7.5% + 5%**. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay))

## 2) Set up the accounting accounts in Xero

In **Xero > Accounting > Advanced > Chart of accounts**, create or check these accounts:

**Expense accounts**
- Salaries / Wages expense
- Employer CPF expense
- SDL expense, if you track Skills Development Levy separately
- Other payroll costs, if applicable

**Liability accounts**
- Net wages payable / Payroll payable
- CPF payable
- SDL payable, if separate
- Other deductions payable, if any

Key point: **employee CPF is not an extra company expense**. It is deducted from the employee’s gross salary. **Employer CPF is the company’s additional payroll expense**.

## 3) Connect a Singapore payroll app to Xero

In Xero, go to the **Xero App Store** and choose a Singapore payroll app that supports CPF calculations and Xero syncing. Xero specifically lists apps such as **Talenox, HReasily, and SimplePay** for Singapore payroll workflows. ([xero.com](https://www.xero.com/sg/accounting-software/payroll/))

Inside the payroll app, set up:

- Company UEN
- CPF Submission Number
- Payroll frequency, usually monthly
- Pay date
- Bank/payment details
- Xero connection
- Chart of account mapping:
  - Gross salary → Salaries / Wages expense
  - Employer CPF → Employer CPF expense
  - Employee CPF + Employer CPF → CPF payable
  - Net salary → Net wages payable or bank clearing
  - SDL → SDL expense / SDL payable, if applicable

## 4) Set up each employee’s CPF profile

For each employee in the payroll app, enter:

- Date of birth — CPF rate changes by age group.
- Citizenship status — Singapore Citizen, SPR, or foreign employee.
- PR start/conversion date — important for 1st-year and 2nd-year SPR rates.
- Salary and recurring allowances.
- Whether each pay item is CPF-bearing.
- Whether payments are **Ordinary Wages** or **Additional Wages**.

CPF Board explains that CPF is calculated on Total Wages, made up of **Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages**, subject to the relevant ceilings. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay))

## 5) Run payroll and check CPF

Each month:

1. Enter salary, allowances, overtime, bonus, unpaid leave, claims, etc.
2. Review CPF calculations.
3. Check that:
   - Foreign employees are not given CPF by mistake.
   - 1st- and 2nd-year SPRs are on the correct contribution rate.
   - Bonuses are treated as Additional Wages.
   - Reimbursements are excluded from CPF where appropriate.
4. Approve the pay run.
5. Post or sync the payroll journal to Xero.
6. Pay employees their net salary.
7. Submit and pay CPF through CPF EZPay, One-Stop Payroll, or your payroll app if supported.

CPF contributions are due on the **last day of the calendar month**, and enforcement action can apply if not paid by the **14th of the following month**, or the next working day if the 14th falls on a weekend/public holiday. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/making-cpf-contributions))

## 6) Example Xero journal for CPF payroll

Example: Employee under 55, Singapore Citizen, gross salary **$5,000**.

- Employee CPF: 20% = **$1,000**
- Employer CPF: 17% = **$850**
- Net salary paid to employee: **$4,000**
- CPF payable to CPF Board: **$1,850**

Journal:

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Salaries / Wages expense | 5,000 |  |
| Employer CPF expense | 850 |  |
| Net wages payable |  | 4,000 |
| CPF payable |  | 1,850 |

When you pay salary:

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Net wages payable | 4,000 |  |
| Bank |  | 4,000 |

When you pay CPF:

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---|---:|---:|
| CPF payable | 1,850 |  |
| Bank |  | 1,850 |

## Practical recommendation

Use a Singapore payroll app integrated with Xero, rather than trying to maintain CPF manually in Xero. CPF rates, PR-year rules, OW/AW ceilings, and age-band changes are easy to get wrong, especially with bonuses, new PRs, or employees crossing age bands. CPF Board also notes that CPF EZPay can auto-compute contributions, and payroll systems can submit wage information through One-Stop Payroll. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/making-cpf-contributions))

---

## 1. What is InvoiceNow?

**InvoiceNow** is not just emailing a PDF invoice. It is a structured, system-to-system e-invoice exchange network. An invoice is created in your accounting, finance, or ERP system, converted into a standard Peppol format, routed through accredited Access Points, and delivered into the recipient’s accounting/ERP system. ([imda.gov.sg](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/peppol-technical-playbook?utm_source=openai))

In practical terms, InvoiceNow lets businesses:

- send invoices directly from one finance system to another;
- reduce manual data entry;
- reduce invoice errors and reconciliation work;
- speed up invoice processing and payment cycles;
- comply with Singapore’s phased GST InvoiceNow Requirement, if GST-registered. ([imda.gov.sg](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/invoicenow?utm_source=openai))

---

## 2. Key parties and terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **InvoiceNow** | Singapore’s nationwide e-invoicing network. |
| **Peppol** | The international interoperability framework used by InvoiceNow. |
| **Peppol ID** | A unique identifier used to receive e-invoices on the network; in Singapore, businesses are registered in the SG Peppol Directory using their UEN. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement)) |
| **Access Point Provider / AP** | An IMDA-accredited provider that connects businesses and software to the Peppol/InvoiceNow network. |
| **InvoiceNow-Ready Solution Provider / IRSP** | An accredited accounting/finance/ERP solution provider connected to InvoiceNow via an accredited AP. ([imda.gov.sg](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/becoming-an-invoicenow-ready-solution-provider?utm_source=openai)) |
| **GST InvoiceNow Requirement** | IRAS requirement for GST-registered businesses to transmit invoice data to IRAS through InvoiceNow-Ready Solutions. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement)) |
| **Solution-extracted invoice** | Invoice data extracted from your accounting/ERP system and submitted through the InvoiceNow network, including for transactions not sent to customers through InvoiceNow. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/etaxguide_gst_invoicenow_requirement.pdf?sfvrsn=d2828aad_35)) |

---

## 3. How InvoiceNow works

InvoiceNow uses the Peppol **4-corner model**:

1. **Supplier / seller** creates an invoice in its system.  
2. The supplier’s **Access Point** converts and sends the invoice in Peppol format.  
3. The buyer’s **Access Point** receives it.  
4. The **buyer** receives the invoice in its own accounting/ERP system. ([imda.gov.sg](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/peppol-technical-playbook?utm_source=openai))

For the GST InvoiceNow Requirement, this model is extended so that invoice data can also be transmitted to **IRAS** through the InvoiceNow network. IMDA describes this as extending the traditional 4-corner model to include a fifth corner for IRAS invoice data submission. ([imda.gov.sg](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/peppol-technical-playbook?utm_source=openai))

---

## 4. Is InvoiceNow mandatory?

### For non-GST-registered businesses

If your business is **not GST-registered**, InvoiceNow is generally not mandatory for GST reporting purposes. However, you may still adopt it voluntarily, especially if your customers, suppliers, or government-sector buyers prefer or require e-invoices.

### For GST-registered businesses

For GST-registered businesses, InvoiceNow is becoming mandatory in phases under the **GST InvoiceNow Requirement**. IRAS states that all GST-registered businesses must submit invoice data to IRAS using InvoiceNow-Ready Solutions, with implementation rolled out progressively. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 5. Mandatory GST InvoiceNow timeline

| Implementation date | Businesses affected |
|---:|---|
| **1 Nov 2025** | Companies that register for GST voluntarily within 6 months of incorporation. |
| **1 Apr 2026** | Businesses that apply for voluntary GST registration on or after this date, regardless of incorporation date or business structure. |
| **1 Apr 2028** | Businesses applying for compulsory GST registration on or after this date; and existing GST-registered businesses with total annual supplies ≤ **S$200,000**. |
| **1 Apr 2029** | Existing GST-registered businesses with total annual supplies ≤ **S$1,000,000**. |
| **1 Apr 2030** | Existing GST-registered businesses with total annual supplies ≤ **S$4,000,000**. |
| **1 Apr 2031** | Existing GST-registered businesses with total annual supplies > **S$4,000,000**. |

For existing GST-registered businesses, “total annual supplies” refers to the total value of standard-rated, zero-rated, and exempt supplies — Box 4 of the GST return — made in prescribed accounting periods ending in calendar year 2025. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 6. Who is excluded?

IRAS excludes the following from the GST InvoiceNow Requirement:

- **overseas entities**, including overseas vendors registered under the Overseas Vendor Registration regimes; and
- businesses liable to register for GST wholly due to the **Reverse Charge** regime. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

However, IRAS clarifies that foreign-incorporated businesses with a local Singapore branch or establishment, and local Singapore businesses with overseas branches, are not automatically treated as excluded overseas entities. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/etaxguide_gst_invoicenow_requirement.pdf?sfvrsn=d2828aad_35))

---

## 7. What invoice data must be submitted to IRAS?

In general, GST-registered businesses subject to the requirement must submit invoice data for transactions reported in their GST returns, including:

- standard-rated supplies;
- zero-rated supplies;
- exempt supplies;
- standard-rated purchases;
- zero-rated purchases. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

This includes data from documents that function as bills for payment or adjustments, such as:

- sales invoices;
- tax invoices;
- simplified tax invoices;
- serially numbered receipts;
- debit notes;
- credit notes. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 8. What invoice data is not required?

IRAS says invoice data for the following transactions need not be submitted:

- transactions with no underlying supplies or purchases but reported for GST purposes, such as deemed supplies and goods exported without sales;
- reverse charge transactions;
- exempt financial services and exchange or loan of digital payment tokens;
- import permits for importation of goods. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 9. Submission deadline to IRAS

Invoice data must be submitted to IRAS by the **earlier of**:

1. the date the relevant GST return is filed; or  
2. the filing due date of the relevant GST return. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

The “relevant GST return” is the GST return for the prescribed accounting period in which the transaction occurs. For supplies where an invoice is or will be issued, the transaction date is generally the document issuance date; for purchases, it can be the supplier document date or the date the transaction is posted into the accounting system, depending on how the business claims input tax. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 10. Types of submissions to IRAS

IRAS identifies four broad submission types:

| Type | Scenario | How it is submitted |
|---|---|---|
| **Type 1A** | Supplier makes a supply transaction within the InvoiceNow network. | Peppol invoice submission. |
| **Type 1B** | Customer records the corresponding purchase transaction received within InvoiceNow. | Solution-extracted invoice submission. |
| **Type 2** | Supplier makes a supply transaction outside InvoiceNow, e.g. customer is not on the network. | Solution-extracted invoice submission. |
| **Type 3** | Customer records a purchase transaction made outside InvoiceNow. | Solution-extracted invoice submission. | ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/etaxguide_gst_invoicenow_requirement.pdf?sfvrsn=d2828aad_35))

This means that even if your customer or supplier is not on InvoiceNow, your GST InvoiceNow-Ready Solution may still need to extract and transmit the relevant invoice data to IRAS. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/etaxguide_gst_invoicenow_requirement.pdf?sfvrsn=d2828aad_35))

---

## 11. How to get started

### If you use off-the-shelf accounting or finance software

1. **Check whether your software is InvoiceNow-Ready.** Use an IMDA-accredited InvoiceNow-Ready Solution where possible.  
2. **Get a Peppol ID.** Ask your solution provider or Access Point to register your business in the SG Peppol Directory using your UEN.  
3. **Activate GST InvoiceNow submission.** Your software provider should help activate the feature to submit invoice data to IRAS. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

### If you use your own ERP or in-house finance system

1. Contact an IMDA-accredited **Access Point Provider**.  
2. Ask the AP to register your business in the SG Peppol Directory using your UEN.  
3. Work with the AP to connect your ERP or in-house system to InvoiceNow and IRAS submission flows.  
4. Activate the GST InvoiceNow submission feature. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

IRAS says onboarding may take as little as **3 months**, while most businesses complete setup within **a year**, depending on readiness and system configuration. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 12. What you need before onboarding

Prepare the following:

- your company or business **UEN**;
- **Corppass** access for authorised users;
- current accounting/ERP system details;
- list of sales channels, POS systems, e-commerce platforms, and billing tools;
- GST registration status and effective GST registration date;
- customer and supplier master data;
- invoice templates and tax codes;
- chart of accounts and GST codes;
- AP/AR workflows;
- staff who will approve, issue, receive, and reconcile invoices.

Singapore-registered businesses need Corppass to complete KYC before transacting on InvoiceNow. ([imda.gov.sg](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/invoicenow?utm_source=openai))

---

## 13. Grants and free solutions

IRAS lists the following support measures:

| Eligible business | Support |
|---|---|
| SMEs with annual supplies ≤ S$4,000,000 | GST InvoiceNow Transition Grant: **S$1,000** |
| Larger businesses with annual supplies > S$4,000,000 | GST InvoiceNow Transition Grant: **S$5,000** |
| Larger businesses with annual turnover > S$4,000,000 | InvoiceNow Queen Bee Grant: **S$25,000** | ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

Free-of-charge solution packages are available up to **31 March 2031** to provide basic e-invoicing capabilities for compliance with the GST InvoiceNow Requirement. Current FOC packages are available for GST-registered businesses until **31 March 2027**, with the list for 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2031 to be made available later. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 14. InvoiceNow and government vendors

If you sell to the Singapore Government, InvoiceNow is increasingly important. IMDA states that the Government will implement InvoiceNow as the default e-invoice submission channel for all government vendors that are registered businesses within the next few years, eventually replacing Vendors@Gov for that group. ([imda.gov.sg](https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/invoicenow?utm_source=openai))

---

## 15. Practical implementation checklist

### Phase 1 — Assess

- Confirm whether you are GST-registered.
- Determine your mandatory implementation date.
- If already GST-registered, check your 2025 total annual supplies.
- Identify all invoicing sources: accounting system, ERP, POS, e-commerce, spreadsheets, manual invoices.
- Identify whether you issue tax invoices, simplified tax invoices, receipts, debit notes, and credit notes.

### Phase 2 — Select solution

- If you use cloud accounting software, confirm it is InvoiceNow-Ready.
- If you use ERP, engage an accredited Access Point.
- Check whether the solution supports:
  - sending Peppol invoices;
  - receiving Peppol invoices;
  - GST InvoiceNow submission to IRAS;
  - credit notes and debit notes;
  - POS aggregation;
  - GST category codes;
  - validation checks;
  - audit logs.

### Phase 3 — Clean data

- Review customer names and UENs.
- Review supplier names and UENs.
- Map GST codes correctly.
- Remove duplicate customer/supplier records.
- Standardise invoice fields, payment terms, and billing addresses.
- Make sure credit notes reference original invoices where required.

### Phase 4 — Configure

- Register for a Peppol ID.
- Connect your system to the Access Point.
- Activate sending and receiving through InvoiceNow.
- Activate IRAS invoice data submission, if GST-registered and required.
- Configure GST categories and tax codes.
- Configure approval workflows.

### Phase 5 — Test

- Send test invoices.
- Receive test invoices.
- Test credit notes.
- Test invoices for GST and non-GST customers.
- Test zero-rated and exempt supplies, if applicable.
- Test POS or simplified tax invoice aggregation, if applicable.
- Confirm that submission data reconciles with GST return values.

### Phase 6 — Go live

- Notify customers and suppliers of your Peppol ID.
- Update purchase orders, onboarding forms, and vendor records.
- Train finance, sales, procurement, and operations teams.
- Monitor failed transmissions or rejected invoices.
- Reconcile GST return figures with transmitted invoice data.

---

## 16. Common mistakes to avoid

1. **Assuming PDF invoices are e-invoices.** A PDF sent by email is not the same as a structured InvoiceNow/Peppol e-invoice.  
2. **Waiting until the deadline.** IRAS says onboarding can take months, and complex ERP environments may need longer. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))  
3. **Ignoring non-InvoiceNow transactions.** Transactions outside the InvoiceNow network may still need to be submitted through solution-extracted invoice data. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/etaxguide_gst_invoicenow_requirement.pdf?sfvrsn=d2828aad_35))  
4. **Not cleaning master data.** Incorrect UENs, customer records, and supplier records can cause routing, reconciliation, and GST reporting problems.  
5. **Forgetting credit notes and debit notes.** Credit notes follow the same broad transmission approach as invoice data. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/etaxguide_gst_invoicenow_requirement.pdf?sfvrsn=d2828aad_35))  
6. **Assuming IRAS submission replaces GST filing.** Businesses remain responsible for accurate GST returns, keeping proper records for at least 5 years, and complying with invoicing rules. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## 17. Recommended action plan by business type

### Small non-GST-registered business

- You are likely not mandated yet.
- Consider adopting InvoiceNow if customers request it.
- Monitor GST registration threshold.
- Use a low-cost or free accounting solution that is InvoiceNow-ready, especially if you expect to register for GST later.

### New voluntary GST registrant

- If applying for voluntary GST registration on or after **1 April 2026**, you must comply with GST InvoiceNow from your effective GST registration date. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/etaxguide_gst_invoicenow_requirement.pdf?sfvrsn=d2828aad_35))  
- Choose an InvoiceNow-Ready Solution before or during the GST registration process.
- Do not wait until after approval to start system setup.

### Existing GST-registered SME

- Check your implementation date based on 2025 total annual supplies.
- Consider early onboarding, especially if you issue many invoices or use multiple sales channels.
- Explore the S$1,000 transition grant or FOC packages if eligible. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

### Larger enterprise

- Treat this as a finance, tax, IT, and data project — not just a tax filing change.
- Map all ERP, POS, billing, procurement, and shared-service workflows.
- Engage APs and solution providers early.
- Plan for integration testing, user acceptance testing, and change management.

---

## 18. Quick compliance checklist

Before your mandatory date, confirm that:

- [ ] You know your GST InvoiceNow implementation date.  
- [ ] Your accounting/ERP system is InvoiceNow-Ready or connected to an accredited AP.  
- [ ] Your business has a Peppol ID.  
- [ ] Your business is registered in the SG Peppol Directory.  
- [ ] GST codes are correctly mapped.  
- [ ] Your system can submit supply and purchase data to IRAS.  
- [ ] Your system handles credit notes and debit notes.  
- [ ] POS, simplified tax invoice, and petty cash aggregation rules are understood.  
- [ ] Finance staff know how to manage failed submissions.  
- [ ] GST return values can be reconciled to invoice data submitted through InvoiceNow.  
- [ ] Records are retained for at least 5 years. ([iras.gov.sg](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-%28gst%29/gst-invoicenow-requirement))

---

## Bottom line

InvoiceNow is Singapore’s Peppol-based e-invoicing network. For many businesses, it is a productivity tool; for GST-registered businesses, it is also becoming a compliance requirement. The most important steps are to determine your mandatory date, select an InvoiceNow-Ready solution or Access Point, obtain your Peppol ID, clean your invoice data, test submissions, and go live well before the deadline.

一般来说，**可以合法**。在新加坡 PDPA 下，公司把员工资料存放在海外 SaaS / 云服务器上**并非当然违法**；关键在于公司是否满足 PDPA 的跨境传输、通知、保护、保留及供应商管理义务。以下是实务判断框架（非正式法律意见）。

## 结论

**合法的典型前提是：**

1. 员工资料的收集、使用、披露是为了合理的人事/雇佣管理目的；
2. 公司已向员工通知相关目的；
3. 海外 SaaS 供应商及其数据中心/分包商受到可执行的义务约束，能提供与 PDPA 相当的保护；
4. 公司与 SaaS 供应商有书面合同/数据处理条款；
5. 公司采取合理安全措施，并管理保留期限、访问权限、数据泄露通知等义务。

PDPC 的指引明确说，雇主为进入、管理或终止雇佣关系而收集、使用、披露员工个人资料，若属合理范围，通常**不需要员工同意**，但仍须通知员工相关目的。([pdpc.gov.sg](https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/-/media/files/pdpc/pdf-files/advisory-guidelines/ag-on-selected-topics/advisory-guidelines-on-the-pdpa-for-selected-topics-%28revised-may-2024%29.pdf))

## 海外 SaaS 的核心问题：Transfer Limitation Obligation

PDPA 第 26 条规定，机构不得把个人资料转移到新加坡境外，除非符合规定要求，以确保境外资料获得与 PDPA 相当的保护。([sso.agc.gov.sg](https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012?ProvIds=P16-&ValidDate=20251205&utm_source=openai)) PDPC 对云服务的指引也说明：如果公司使用云服务供应商处理个人资料，公司仍需对该个人资料遵守 PDPA；即使云服务商在新加坡或海外，公司仍负责跨境传输义务。([pdpc.gov.sg](https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/-/media/files/pdpc/pdf-files/advisory-guidelines/ag-on-selected-topics/advisory-guidelines-on-the-pdpa-for-selected-topics-%28revised-may-2024%29.pdf))

实务上，公司通常需要确保 SaaS 供应商：

- 只把数据转移到有可比较数据保护制度的地点；**或**
- 通过合同、认证或其他法律上可执行的义务，承诺提供与 PDPA 相当的保护。([pdpc.gov.sg](https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/-/media/files/pdpc/pdf-files/advisory-guidelines/ag-on-selected-topics/advisory-guidelines-on-the-pdpa-for-selected-topics-%28revised-may-2024%29.pdf))

PDPC 还指出，合同最好处理两个问题：**保护标准**以及**海外地点**；如果涉及海外数据中心或 sub-processors，也应覆盖这些接收方。([pdpc.gov.sg](https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/-/media/files/pdpc/pdf-files/advisory-guidelines/ag-on-selected-topics/advisory-guidelines-on-the-pdpa-for-selected-topics-%28revised-may-2024%29.pdf))

## 公司应检查什么？

建议公司至少做以下合规检查：

| 项目 | 要点 |
|---|---|
| **员工通知** | 员工手册、雇佣合同、隐私通知中是否说明资料会用于 HR、薪资、福利、考勤、绩效、IT 管理等目的，并可能披露给第三方服务商/境外供应商。 |
| **SaaS 合同** | 是否有 DPA / data processing agreement、保密义务、安全措施、子处理商控制、审计或报告权、数据删除/返还条款。 |
| **跨境传输条款** | 是否列明数据存放/处理国家，或要求供应商及其数据中心、sub-processors 提供 PDPA 相当保护。 |
| **安全措施** | MFA、最小权限、加密、访问日志、备份、漏洞管理、供应商安全认证如 ISO 27001 / SOC 2 等。 |
| **保留期限** | 员工离职后资料不能无限期保留；应基于业务或法律目的保留。 |
| **数据泄露流程** | 若发生可通知的数据泄露，公司可能需要评估并通知 PDPC/受影响个人。 |
| **敏感资料** | NRIC、薪资、医疗、纪律记录、绩效评估等应有更高保护。 |

## 员工是否可以反对“资料在海外”？

不一定。若公司是为合理的人事管理目的使用 SaaS，且已满足 PDPA 的通知和跨境传输要求，员工通常不能仅因服务器在海外就主张违法。但员工可要求公司说明：

- 资料为何被收集/使用/披露；
- 资料会被披露给哪些类别的第三方；
- 是否有跨境传输及相应保护措施；
- 如何访问或更正个人资料；
- DPO 的联系方式。

## 什么时候可能违法？

以下情况风险较高：

- 公司没有告知员工资料会被披露给 SaaS/第三方；
- 没有与 SaaS 供应商签署足够的数据保护条款；
- 不知道数据实际存放在哪些国家或由哪些 sub-processors 处理；
- 供应商无合理安全措施或认证；
- 员工资料被用于与雇佣管理无关的新目的，例如营销、画像、商业分析，而未取得适当同意或没有其他合法依据；
- 离职员工资料长期无限期保留；
- 发生泄露后未按 PDPA 评估/通知。

**一句话：**在 PDPA 下，把员工资料放在海外 SaaS 服务器上通常是可以的，但公司必须证明其已做好通知、供应商合同、跨境传输保护、安全与保留管理；否则就可能构成 PDPA 违规。

## Checklist: Switching payroll software in Singapore mid-year

Use this as a **cutover checklist** for a Singapore employer moving payroll systems partway through a calendar year.

### 1. Plan the cutover

- [ ] Choose a **cutover date** preferably at the start of a payroll month, after the prior month’s payroll is fully completed.
- [ ] Avoid switching in the middle of an open payroll period unless the new system can handle part-month proration cleanly.
- [ ] Decide which system is the **system of record** for:
  - Employee master data
  - Salary and pay items
  - CPF / SDL / SHG contributions
  - Leave balances
  - Claims and reimbursements
  - IRAS year-end reporting
- [ ] Assign owners for HR, payroll, finance, IT, and vendor implementation.
- [ ] Freeze payroll master-data changes during migration, except urgent starters/leavers/salary changes.

---

- [ ] **CPF calculations** by age, citizenship, Singapore PR year, Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. - [ ] **Self-Help Group contributions** — CDAC, MBMF, SINDA, ECF — where applicable. ([cpf.gov.sg](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups?utm_source=openai))
- [ ] CPF submission file / CPF EZPay integration or export.

### 4. Prepare opening balances in the new system

This is the most important mid-year step.

For each employee, load year-to-date figures from **1 January to the cutover date**, including:

- [ ] Gross salary.
- [ ] Basic salary.
- [ ] Fixed allowances.
- [ ] Variable allowances.

**Short answer:** In air purifiers, **“HEPA”** should mean the filter meets a recognized HEPA efficiency standard, while **“True HEPA”** is mostly a **marketing term** used to signal that the purifier uses a real HEPA-grade filter—not a “HEPA-type” or “HEPA-like” filter.

### Key difference

| Term | What it usually means | Important note |
|---|---|---|
| **HEPA** | A high-efficiency particulate air filter. In the U.S., commonly associated with capturing **99.97% of particles at 0.3 microns**. | This is the actual technical category. |
| **True HEPA** | Usually means the same thing as real HEPA: **99.97% at 0.3 microns**. | Not a separate official standard in many markets; often used to distinguish from weaker “HEPA-type” filters. |
| **HEPA-type / HEPA-like** | Looks or sounds like HEPA but may not meet true HEPA performance. | Often less effective; check the actual stated efficiency. |

### What you should look for

When buying an air purifier, don’t rely only on the phrase **“True HEPA.”** Check for:

1. **Filtration rating**  
   Look for something like **99.97% at 0.3 microns** or standards such as **H13/H14 HEPA**.

2. **CADR rating**  
   This tells you how much clean air the purifier delivers. A real HEPA filter with a weak fan may still perform poorly in a large room.

3. **Room size coverage**  
   Make sure the purifier is rated for your room size.

4. **Sealed filter design**  
   If air can leak around the filter, even a good HEPA filter won’t perform as well.

### Bottom line

**“HEPA” and “True HEPA” often mean the same thing**, but **“True HEPA” is mainly a marketing label**. The bigger thing to avoid is **“HEPA-type” or “HEPA-like”**, which may not meet real HEPA filtration standards.
